## Check your factorisation

Factorise $18x^2-50$ fully on paper. Select the fully factorised answer.

<div class="index-check" role="group" aria-label="Choose the fully factorised expression">

<button type="button" data-choice="a" aria-pressed="false">A. $2(9x^2-25)$</button>
<button type="button" data-choice="b" aria-pressed="false">B. $(3x-5)(3x+5)$</button>
<button type="button" data-choice="c" aria-pressed="false">C. $2(3x-5)^2$</button>
<button type="button" data-choice="d" aria-pressed="false">D. $2(3x-5)(3x+5)$</button>

</div>

<div class="check-feedback" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">
<div data-result="a" hidden>

You found the highest common factor. Look inside the bracket. Can you factorise the difference of two squares? Try again.

</div>
<div data-result="b" hidden>

Your brackets expand to $9x^2-25$. Compare the coefficients with $18x^2-50$. Which factor belongs in front? Try again.

</div>
<div data-result="c" hidden>

Identical brackets give a non-zero middle term here. The original expression has no term in $x$. Check the signs and try again.

</div>
<div data-result="d" hidden>

**Correct.** Take out 2, then factorise the difference of two squares.

$18x^2-50=2(9x^2-25)=2(3x-5)(3x+5)$.

</div>
</div>

<button class="reset-check" type="button" hidden>Try again from the start</button>
